instructions: Choose, type or arrange the correct participle form used as an adjective.

items.explanation: Past participle begeistert (enthusiastic) used as an adjective; after das in the nominative singular the ending is -e.
lachen + d = lachend (an action happening now); after der in the nominative singular masculine the ending is -e.
Past participle belegt (a filled roll); after ein, a neuter noun in the accusative needs -es.
bellen + d = bellend; after einen (masculine accusative) the ending is -en.
With no article, the adjective shows the case itself: neuter nominative/accusative = -es (fließendes Wasser).
The car has been sold (passive, completed), so use the past participle verkauft + -e after das; verkaufende would mean the car itself is selling.
Past participle of zerbrechen (irregular: zerbrochen); after die in the plural accusative the ending is -en.
warten + d = wartend (the taxi that is waiting); after dem in the dative singular the ending is always -en.
A phone that has been lost: past participle verloren; after mein, neuter accusative takes -es.
spielen + d = spielend (children who are playing); after die in the plural nominative the ending is -en.
Past participle verletzt (injured); after der in the feminine dative the ending is -en.

items.prompt: Das Spielzeug des ___ Kindes ist kaputt.
items.explanation: After des (genitive singular) the adjective ending is -en: des weinenden Kindes.
Past participle with un- (ungelöst = not solved); after ein, neuter nominative needs -es.

items.prompt: Der vor der Tür ___ Mann ist mein Nachbar.
items.explanation: In an extended participial phrase, the participle stands right before the noun with the adjective ending: der vor der Tür stehende Mann (nominative, -e).

items.prompt: Das von Anna ___ Foto hängt an der Wand.
items.explanation: The photo was taken by Anna: past participle with -e after das (nominative neuter); the phrase von Anna belongs before it.
Past participle gebacken, plus -es after ein (neuter accusative): ein frisch gebackenes Brot.

items.prompt: Die ___ Sonne weckt mich jeden Morgen.
items.explanation: Present participle = infinitive + d (aufgehend, the prefix stays attached); after die in the feminine nominative add -e.
fahren + d = fahrend (a moving train); after einen in the masculine accusative the ending is -en.
Verbs in -ieren form the past participle without ge-: möbliert; after ein, neuter accusative adds -es.

items.prompt: Ich gebe der ___ Frau die Hand.
items.explanation: lächeln + d = lächelnd; after der in the feminine dative the ending is -en.

items.prompt: Ein ___ Computer ist billiger als ein neuer.
items.explanation: Past participle gebraucht (used, second-hand); after ein in the masculine nominative the ending is -er.
Present participle fliehend (or flüchtend) takes -en after den (masculine accusative).
Irregular past participle geliehen (borrowed); after ein, neuter accusative adds -es.
ankommen + d = ankommend (the guests who are arriving); after den in the dative plural the ending is -en.
Without an article, plural accusative takes -e: motivierte Mitarbeiter (motivieren forms motiviert, no ge-).

items.prompt: Der seit zwei Jahren hier ___ Student kommt aus Spanien.
items.explanation: In an extended phrase the participle stands directly before the noun with its ending: der ... hier wohnende Student.

items.prompt: Die von der Firma ___ Waren sind teuer.
items.explanation: Past participle with a von-phrase in front of it; after die in the plural nominative the ending is -en.

items.prompt: Das ___ Paket liegt vor der Tür.
items.explanation: bestellen has an inseparable prefix, so the past participle is bestellt (no ge-); after das in the nominative neuter add -e.

answers: Der schlafende Hund liegt im Garten.
items.translation: The sleeping dog is lying in the garden.
items.explanation: The participle schlafende stands between the article and the noun, like any adjective.

answers: Die vor dem Kino wartenden Leute frieren.
items.translation: The people waiting in front of the cinema are cold.
items.explanation: In an extended participial phrase, the extra information (vor dem Kino) goes between the article die and the participle wartenden, which stands right before the noun.
